subject: Astronomy & Space
title: William Herschel: Discovering Uranus
description: A quick, practical guide to William Herschel: Discovering Uranus.

hook.text: In 1781, a musician-turned-astronomer found a new planet. It was the first planet discovered since antiquity.

buildup.text: William Herschel built his own telescopes. His 40-foot reflector was the largest in the world at the time.

discovery.text: He initially thought Uranus was a comet. Calculations proved it was a planet orbiting beyond Saturn.

twist.text: Herschel wanted to name it 'Georgium Sidus' after King George III. The international community chose 'Uranus' instead.

climax.text: He also discovered infrared radiation by splitting sunlight with a prism. A musician who changed two fields of science.

punchline.text: A musician found a planet. Then he discovered invisible light.

quiz.question: What did William Herschel discover besides Uranus?
options: Infrared radiation, by measuring heat beyond the red end of the spectrum
The rings of Saturn and their composition
The first asteroid in the asteroid belt

details.summary: William Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781 — the first planet found since antiquity. Using a homemade 6.2-inch reflector telescope, he initially thought it was a comet.
details.whyItMatters: Discovering Uranus proved the solar system was bigger than anyone imagined and that new worlds could still be found. It inspired a new era of systematic sky surveys and eventually led to the discoveries of Neptune and beyond.
takeaways: Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781 using a homemade telescope
It was the first planet found since antiquity
The discovery doubled the known size of the solar system

faq.question: How did Herschel discover Uranus?
faq.answer: During a systematic survey of the sky on March 13, 1781, Herschel noticed an object that appeared as a disk rather than a point of light. He initially reported it as a comet. Over weeks, other astronomers calculated its orbit and realized it was a new planet — the first discovered with a telescope.

faq.question: What else did Herschel discover?
faq.answer: Herschel discovered infrared radiation, cataloged over 2,500 nebulae and star clusters, discovered two moons of Uranus and two of Saturn, and was the first to correctly suggest the Milky Way is disk-shaped. His sister Caroline was also a noted astronomer who discovered several comets.
